verification_decisions.reason: The code contains 'or True' in the exception check condition, causing all exceptions during parallel research execution to unconditionally trigger workflow termination.
During research compression, token limit checking incorrectly inspects configurable.research_model instead of configurable.compression_model, which can cause misclassification when models differ.
This is a duplicate claim of finding d96300f55fb3, identifying the exact same cause (the 'or True' condition on line 334) and consequence.

findings.title: Unconditional exception termination in supervisor research error handling
findings.impact: Any exception during parallel research execution causes the research phase to terminate prematurely instead of handling or retrying.
findings.preconditions: An exception is raised during research execution in supervisor_tools.
findings.explanation: The exception handler condition includes `or True`, making it unconditionally evaluate to True and forcing early workflow termination on any exception regardless of whether a token limit was exceeded.
findings.suggestion: Update the exception handler condition to remove 'or True': except Exception as e: if is_token_limit_exceeded(e, configurable.research_model): return Command(goto=END, update={"notes": get_notes_from_tool_calls(supervisor_messages), "research_brief": state.get("research_brief", "")}); raise e. Regression test: assert that non-token-limit exceptions propagate correctly rather than terminating the workflow.

findings.impact: Token limit exceptions during compression may fail to be correctly detected if compression_model differs from research_model.
findings.preconditions: An exception occurs during research compression using synthesizer_model configured with compression_model.
findings.explanation: The exception handler calls `is_token_limit_exceeded(e, configurable.research_model)` instead of using `configurable.compression_model`.
findings.suggestion: Pass configurable.compression_model instead of configurable.research_model to is_token_limit_exceeded in compress_research: if is_token_limit_exceeded(e, configurable.compression_model): researcher_messages = remove_up_to_last_ai_message(researcher_messages); continue. Regression test: verify compression token limit check uses compression model config.

findings.title: Unconditional exception fallback masking all runtime errors
findings.impact: Any exception occurring during parallel research execution is unconditionally caught and treated as a normal token-limit termination event, masking bugs and unexpected failures.
findings.preconditions: An exception is raised inside the try block executing research tasks in supervisor_tools.
findings.explanation: The exception handler uses 'if is_token_limit_exceeded(e, configurable.research_model) or True:', which evaluates to True for every exception, swallowing unexpected errors and bypasses standard error propagation.

findings.impact: Application crashes with an IndexError when the research agent model responds without any tool calls.
findings.preconditions: The research agent LLM returns a message lacking tool calls (empty tool_calls list).
findings.explanation: Unlike supervisor_should_continue which guards against empty tool calls, research_agent_should_continue directly indexes last_message.tool_calls[0] without verifying that tool_calls is non-empty.
findings.suggestion: async def research_agent_should_continue(state: SectionState) -> str: messages = state["messages"]; last_message = messages[-1]; if not last_message.tool_calls: return END; if last_message.tool_calls[0]["name"] == "FinishResearch": return END; else: return "research_agent_tools"
